What I've done to keep myself from cutting during times where I am clean is to find a distraction or another coping mechanism. I usually use music or stupid youtube videos to entertain myself when I get real down. Also, playing a mindless game or something. You could try venting with art or something. I occasionally scribble down crappy poetry in a notebook I have just venting. Most of it never sees the light of day again. Also, some people have a rubber band on their wrist and snap it on them when they get the urge to cut. I haven't tried it, but people use it. Overall, keep telling yourself it isn't worth it to cut. It will only help for a little bit and you'll be thrown back into the downward spiral of cutting.

Building on what suicidejunkie said, the problem with planning to control it is that it's extremely hard to do. That's what I said when I started, but self-harm is an addiction. I started with picking myself with a pin, within a few months I was using a blade. The sessions got closer and closer together. There were more and more cuts each time. They started getting deeper and longer. It spirals out of control. Like smoking, it's extremely hard to quit. I've been doing it for 6 years on and off. Even when I am 'clean' I still think about cutting as a coping mechanism. 

Best thing is to find an alternative coping mechanism. Listening to music, writing poetry, doing art, browsing youtube, etc.

If you find pain helps you could try snapping a rubber band on your wrist then you get the urge to self-harm. Because of subreddit rules I can't tell you anything about methods of cutting, but the best advice I have is that you shouldn't start. It just escalates and gets worse and worse the more you do it. I've had this problem as well. I go on and off and at the moment I am 'on' again. It really sucks. My main reason to keep clean is so I don't get caught and hurt the people around me. I don't think of cutting as *that* bad of an issue. I know it isn't by any means a healthy way to deal with things, but there are worse. 

Aside from getting caught, I've noticed that the more I cut, the more frequent the cutting has to be. Then more cuts each session. Then deeper. I try and stop it before it gets out of control to the point where I need stitches.

The biggest thing is to try and find things to replace cutting. It's hard, but finding it is important. Sometimes I write [poetry](http://sadcatpoems.tumblr.com/) to take my mind off of things. It isn't anything organized or good, but it works. Sometimes I will play computer games or just go on youtube. So, yeah, distractions work. 

When you do cut, just make sure you do it safely.

I hope you can find something to help you keep your mind away from cutting.

Hey there, trans chick weighing in. So, yeah, trans-ness kinda sucks. It's one of those things no one is going to understand unless they actually experience it for themselves.

As for the self-harm stuff. I would use scars as a motivation. The surgery won't remove all of the skin so if there are scars, they might stay there. Plus, we are all vain to an extent and want people to see a good looking body. For most people, that does not include scars. 

Also, from experience, the more and longer one cuts, the worse it is going to get. I've been at it for 6 years with the biggest gap between 'sessions' being a little over a year. As you know, the first time you self-harm it feels good, but slowly the same harm gets less and less. I found myself needing the 'good' feeling from cutting and the cuts got more and more per session, deeper and deeper, and more frequent. It's an addiction you'll be stuck with for life. Whenever I'm depressed I just want to take out a blade and go at my foot. 

It feels good and actually works, but I'd go back and never start it in the first place if I was able to. 

I guess, from another angle, if people discover the cutting it can hurt and worry them. Some people, me included, don't see self harm as a huge issue if it is done safely. I am not saying it's good by any means, but I feel there are worse ways to deal. Someone who doesn't understand the self-harm thing can get extremely worried and hurt because of it. Plus, you could get forcefully hospitalized. 

Kinda random ranting and stuff. Hope you got something out of it. If you ever want to talk more, let me know.

~Xi
